newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Friday:
Spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said there would be a news conference at 1600/1500 GMT at the Council on the addendum to the draft revision of the EU Treaty.
Van der Pas said next week's Commission meeting would take place in Rome on Tuesday afternoon.
Spokespersons Joao Vale de Almeida, Josep Coll i Carbo, Peter Guilford and Lousewies van der Laan briefed on Monday and Tuesday's General Affairs Council.
Vale de Almeida said the Commission was optimistic about reaching an agreement on South Africa's partial accession to the Lome Convention.

Guilford said the Commission was not in favour of a study into the compatibility of the existing free trade agreements with the World Trade Organisation (WTO) nor of a pause in the negotiations on free trade areas.
Guilford also said the EU might introduce a proposal for a United Nations resolution to condemn non-observance of human rights in China.
He also said after EU foreign ministers had given the go-ahead, the International Technology Agreement (ITA) would be formally approved by the WTO on Wednesday.

Van der Laan said the foreign ministers would discuss the situation in Cyprus, Albania and former-Yugoslavia, and the U.S.-Russia summit. She said there would also be a structured dialogue with the Eastern and Central European countries.

Vale de Almeida said Commissioner de Deus Pinheiro's Chef de Cabinet Carlos Costa had met Nigerian Nobel Prize winner Wole Soyinka in Brussels. He said the Commission clearly supported a democratic and peaceful transition in Nigeria.
In answer to a question, Coll i Carbo said non-implementation of the EU-Israel accord was one of the things the EU could do to condemn the continued building of new Israeli settlements.
He also confirmed that the Commission had had to suspend a project with the Mexican Human Rights Academy because the Mexican authorities had not authorised it.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/246: A top-up funding for the Socrates programme.
- Speech/97/68: Speech by Commissioner Padraig Flynn on the fight against racism.
- Specch/97/69: Speech by Commissioner Christos Papoutsis on "towards a Community action plan for renewable energy sources"
- Speech/97/71: Speech by Commission President Jacques Santer on the role of the regions in the European construction.
- Memo/97/30: EU/ South Africa: proposals for long-term co-operation.
- Memo/97/31: Calendar of the Commissioners' activities for March 24-31.
- ME97/21.3: Midday Express.
